title: Engineering of Dual Wavelength, Polarization Selective Metalenses in Silicon Carbide
authors: Xiaoying Huang, Ziwei Yang, Konosuke Shimazaki, Kritsana Saego, Otto Cranwell Schaeper, Evan Williams, Dragomir Neshev, Hark Hoe Tan, Igor Aharonovicha, Mehran Kianinia
abstract: Spin defects in silicon carbide (SiC) are promising candidates for integrated quantum photonics, offering long-lived spin states and near-infrared emission suitable for low-loss photonic integration and fibre-based quantum communication. However, light extraction from these defects remains challenging due the relatively high refractive index of SiC. Metalenses offer a compact approach to enhance light collection by engineering the wavefront directly at the material interface. Here, we design and fabricate monolithic metalenses from SiC bulk material that simultaneously operate at 860 and 1240 nm, matching with emission from the nitrogen vacancy and silicon vacancy colour centers. By independently engineering the phase response at both wavelengths, the metalens enables collection and polarization manipulation of the emitted light. We further employ the metalenses to demonstrate optically detected magnetic resonance of both defects simultaneously. These multifunctional metalenses provide a compact optical interface for scalable integrated SiC photonic devices.
summary: This paper reports the design and fabrication of monolithic metalenses on SiC capable of operating at dual wavelengths (860 nm and 1240 nm). These devices overcome light extraction limitations from embedded quantum emitters by engineering the wavefront, enabling polarization-selective collection and simultaneous readout of spin states from VSi and NV centers.
main_problem: The primary challenge is efficiently extracting and manipulating the polarization of photons emitted from spin defects (like NV and VSi centers) embedded in Silicon Carbide (SiC) for integrated quantum photonics.
main_result: The authors successfully designed and fabricated monolithic metalenses on SiC that simultaneously operate at 860 nm and 1240 nm, enabling polarization-selective collection and demonstration of optically detected magnetic resonance.
method: The research involved designing subwavelength meta-atoms using rigorous simulations (RCWA, FDTD) and fabricating the dual-wavelength metalenses via top-down nanofabrication techniques.
model_or_system: The physical system is a monolithic metalens fabricated on a bulk SiC substrate, engineered to interact with light emitted from implanted VSi and NV color centers. The design allows independent phase control for orthogonal polarization channels at two distinct near-infrared wavelengths.
key_observables: Simultaneous collection efficiency at 860 nm and 1240 nm; polarization separation (H vs. V); successful readout via Optically Detected Magnetic Resonance (ODMR).
important_parameters: Wavelengths: 860 nm and 1240 nm; Meta-atom height: $1.6 \mu	ext{m}$; Collection NA: 0.97.
main_assumptions: The design assumes the ability to independently engineer the phase response at two distinct wavelengths using the same SiC material platform.
figures_summary: Figures show the design concept, calculated phase distributions for H/V polarizations at both wavelengths, and SEM/optical microscope images confirming the fabrication of the monolithic metalens.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the need for enhanced light extraction from SiC defects to detailing the metalens design via simulation, describing the nanofabrication process, and finally demonstrating the multifunctional capabilities through PL spectroscopy and ODMR measurements.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the integration challenge in quantum photonics by providing a scalable, on-chip optical interface that controls both wavelength and polarization, which is crucial for building quantum networks.
